num:vier.tx: From Middle High German vier, from Old High German fior, from Proto-West Germanic *feuwar, from Proto-Germanic *fedwōr, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷetwṓr, the neuter form of *kʷetwóres. Compare Dutch vier, English four, Danish fire, Swedish fyra.

prep:via.tx: Ultimately from Latin viā, the ablative of via (“road, way”). Cognate with English via, Danish via, Dutch via, Norwegian Bokmål via.

noun:Velo.tx: Borrowed from French vélo, or shortened form Veloziped.

verb:verachten.tx: From Middle High German verahten. Equivalent to ver- + achten.

num:vierzehn.tx: From Middle High German vierzehen, from Old High German fiorzehan, from Proto-Germanic *fedurtehun. Equivalent to vier + zehn. Compare Dutch veertien, West Frisian fjirtjin, English fourteen, Danish fjorten, Gothic 𐍆𐌹𐌳𐍅𐍉𐍂𐍄𐌰𐌹𐌷𐌿𐌽 (fidwōrtaihun).

prep:von.tx: From Middle High German von(e) (“from”), from Old High German fon(a), alongside rarer northern fan(a). It is uncertain whether the High German o-vocalism continues an original Proto-Germanic *funē, comparable with Sanskrit पुनः- (punaḥ-), or whether it is an atonic alteration of Proto-West Germanic *fanā. In the latter case, possibly from Proto-Germanic *afa + *ana (equivalent to German ab + an). …

verb:versterben.tx: From Middle High German versterben. By surface analysis, ver- + sterben.

verb:verstehen.tx: From Middle High German verstān, virstēn, vorstēn, ferstān, from Old High German firstān, firstēn, from Proto-Germanic *frastāną, equivalent to ver- + stehen. Cognate with Bavarian versteh, Dutch verstaan, Middle Low German vorstān. Compare also English forstand.

adj:vehement.tx: Ca. 1700, from Latin vehemens, vehementis, in part through French véhément.

noun:Vater.tx: From Middle High German vater, from Old High German fater, from Proto-West Germanic *fader, from Proto-Germanic *fadēr, from Proto-Indo-European *ph₂tḗr. Germanic cognates include Dutch vader, Low German Vader, English father, Danish fader, Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐌳𐌰𐍂 (fadar).

noun:Vogel.tx: From Middle High German vogel, vagel, from Old High German fogal, fugal, from Proto-West Germanic *fugl, from Proto-Germanic *fuglaz; possibly related to *fleuganą (“to fly”) through dissimilation from earlier *fluglaz. Cognates include Low German Vagel, Dutch vogel, English fowl, Danish fugl, Swedish fågel, Gothic 𐍆𐌿𐌲𐌻𐍃 (fugls).

prep:vor.tx: From Middle High German vore, vor, from Old High German fora. Cognate with Dutch voor. Compare English fore.

adj:vogelfrei.tx: 15th century, from Vogel (“bird”) + frei (“free”). The earliest use was of persons who were free from feudal obligation and thus enjoyed freedom of movement. It seems plausible that the use for “outlawed” may be based on this, in the sense that the outlaw is forced ever to move from place to place. However, the predominantly accepted derivation is from the fact that outlaws could not be buried in …

adj:verschieden.tx: From verscheiden in its original sense of "separate, leave".

adv:verschieden.tx: From verscheiden in its original sense of "separate, leave".

adj:voll.tx: From Middle High German vol, from Old High German foll, from Proto-West Germanic *full, from Proto-Germanic *fullaz, from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁nós. Compare Low German vull, Dutch vol, English full, Danish fuld, Swedish full. The stem is spelt with v- before -o-, -ö- (as in voll, Völle, Völlerei), but with f- before -ü- (as in füllen, Fülle). Modern German does not allow v for /f/ before -u-, …

adv:voll.tx: From Middle High German vol, from Old High German foll, from Proto-West Germanic *full, from Proto-Germanic *fullaz, from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁nós. Compare Low German vull, Dutch vol, English full, Danish fuld, Swedish full. The stem is spelt with v- before -o-, -ö- (as in voll, Völle, Völlerei), but with f- before -ü- (as in füllen, Fülle). Modern German does not allow v for /f/ before -u-, …

adj:verboten.tx: From Middle High German verboten, from Old High German firbotan, from Proto-West Germanic *furibodan, from Proto-Germanic *furibudanaz.

noun:Verbrechen.tx: 17th century, nominalised infinitive of verbrechen (now in limited use), from Middle High German verbrechen (“to breach, violate”). Equivalent to ver- + brechen (“to break”).

noun:V.tx: For the origin of the letter, see v. Orthography and pronunciation Germanic f was pronounced [v] in some dialects of Middle High German and was predominantly spelt v. This voicing was later reversed stem-initially in most dialects and stem-internally in some (including Standard German). In inherited words, the spelling mostly switched back to f accordingly. This always happened before l, r, u, ü, …

noun:Vanille.tx: Ca. 1700, borrowed from French vanille, from Spanish vainilla. The pronunciation with /lj/ reflects the older French /ʎ/; that with /l/ is a spelling pronunciation.

noun:Vendetta.tx: Borrowed from Italian vendetta (“revenge”). The more general sense of "grudge" is possibly a semantic loan from English vendetta.

noun:Verb.tx: Adaptation of older Verbum, from Latin verbum (“word”). Doublet of Wort.

noun:Vers.tx: From Middle High German vërs, from Old High German fërs, from Latin versus.

noun:Veto.tx: Borrowed from Latin vetō (“to forbid”) (18th century).

noun:Vier.tx: From Middle High German vier, from Old High German fior.

noun:Villa.tx: Borrowed from Italian villa, from Latin villa.

noun:Viper.tx: Middle High German vip(p)er, vipere, from Latin vīpera.

noun:Visage.tx: 17th century, borrowed from French visage (“face”). Early on often pejoratively, to which context it was ultimately restricted.

noun:Visum.tx: 18th century as Visa, from French visa, from Latin visa, plural of visum (“something seen”). The form was later relatinised yielding the contemporary singular in -um.

noun:Volleyball.tx: Borrowed from English volleyball, equivalent to volley + Ball.

noun:Volt.tx: Named after Italian physicist Alessandro Volta. For the surname, see Italian Volta.

noun:Voodoo.tx: Borrowed from English voodoo, from a West African language.

verb:verstoßen.tx: From Middle High German verstōzen, from Old High German firstōzan. Equivalent to ver- + stoßen.

noun:Vorbote.tx: From Middle High German vorbote, from Old High German foraboto; equivalent to vor- + Bote. Compare English foreboding.

pron:viel.tx: From Middle High German vil, vile, from Old High German filu (“many”), from Proto-West Germanic *felu, from Proto-Germanic *felu, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁-. More at fele.

det:viel.tx: From Middle High German vil, vile, from Old High German filu (“many”), from Proto-West Germanic *felu, from Proto-Germanic *felu, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁-. More at fele.

adv:viel.tx: From Middle High German vil, vile, from Old High German filu (“many”), from Proto-West Germanic *felu, from Proto-Germanic *felu, from Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁-. More at fele.

verb:verlassen.tx: From Middle High German verlāzen, Old High German firlāzan, from Proto-West Germanic *fralātan, from Proto-Germanic *fralētaną. Cognate with Dutch verlaten, archaic and/or dialectal English forlet, and Middle Low German vorlaten. Equivalent to ver- (“for-”) + lassen (“let, leave”).

noun:Verlies.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German verlies (“loss”), cognate with Dutch verlies (“id.”) and German verlieren (“to lose”). Apparently, the original meaning is "place where someone is lost"; possibly a second word (like "place", "hole") has been omitted, although no such compound seems to be attested.

verb:verlieren.tx: From Middle High German verliesen, from Old High German firliosan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraleusan, from Proto-Germanic *fraleusaną, from Proto-Indo-European *leu- (“to detach”). Compare Ancient Greek λύω (lúō, “loose, untie”), Latin solvō (“dissolve”), English forlorn, Dutch verliezen.

verb:verbringen.tx: From Middle High German verbringen, from Old High German firbringan. Equivalent to ver- + bringen.

verb:verringern.tx: From ver- + archaic ringern (“to make lighter, soften, weaken”), a verbal formation from the same root as gering (“little, low”) (see there for more).

noun:Venushügel.tx: Calque of Latin mons veneris, Venus + Hügel.

verb:verhalten.tx: From Middle High German verhalten, from Old High German firhaltan, from Proto-West Germanic *frahaldan, equivalent to ver- + halten. Cognate with Middle Low German vörhōlden, Dutch verhouden, English forhold. Compare Danish forholde sig.

verb:vermeiden.tx: From Middle High German vermīden, from Old High German firmīdan. Equivalent to ver- + meiden.

noun:Vogelspinne.tx: From Vogel (“bird”) + Spinne (“spider”). A calque of Latin Aranea avicularia, coined by Carl Linnaeus in the 10th edition of Systema Naturae (1758, tomus I, p. 619 + 622).

num:vierzig.tx: From Middle High German vierzic, from Old High German fiorzug, from Proto-Germanic *fedwōr tigiwiz, equivalent to vier + -zig.

noun:Vorsteherdrüse.tx: Vorsteher (“one that stands before”) + Drüse (“gland”), the first element being a semantic loan from Latin prostata, itself from Ancient Greek προστάτης (prostátēs).

verb:verschleißen.tx: From Middle High German verslīȥen, from Old High German firslīȥan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraslītan. Cognates include Low German verslieten and Dutch verslijten, also akin to Old English forslītan. Equivalent to ver- + schleißen.

verb:verbrechen.tx: From Middle High German verbrëchen (“to breach, violate”), from Old High German firbrëhhan (“to break, destroy”), from Proto-West Germanic *frabrekan. Equivalent to ver- + brechen. Cognates include Dutch verbreken and English forbreak.

verb:vögeln.tx: From Middle High German vogelen, vogeln, from Old High German fogalōn (“catch birds”). Related to Vogel (“bird”), from Proto-Germanic *fuglaz (“bird”), from Proto-Indo-European *pleu (“to flow, to float”). Cognate with English fowl.

verb:verdienen.tx: From Middle High German verdienen, from Old High German firdionōn, firthiniōn. Equivalent to ver- + dienen, calque of Latin deservio.

noun:Verein.tx: From Middle High German vereine, synchronically analyzed as a deverbal from vereinen.

verb:verleihen.tx: From Middle High German verlīhen, from Old High German firlīhan. Equivalent to ver- + leihen.

verb:vergessen.tx: From Middle High German vergëȥȥen, from Old High German firgëȥȥan, from Proto-West Germanic *fragetan.

adj:vergessen.tx: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

noun:Verso.tx: Borrowed from Latin versō foliō (literally “on the turned page”).

verb:verbieten.tx: From Middle High German verbieten, from Old High German firbiotan, from Proto-West Germanic *furibeudan, from Proto-Germanic *furibeudaną. Equivalent to ver- + bieten. Compare Dutch verbieden, Low German verbeden, English forbid, Danish forbyde, Swedish förbjuda, Gothic 𐍆𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌱𐌹𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (faurbiudan).

verb:verfolgen.tx: ver- + folgen. A calque of Latin persequor or its Romance descendants.

verb:verweisen.tx: From two separate but related verbs. From Middle High German verwīsen (“refer; relegate; expel, banish”), derivative of wīsen, whence German weisen; and the second verb from Middle High German verwīȥen (“blame, accuse”), from Old High German farwīȥan, firwīȥan, from Proto-West Germanic *frawītan, from Proto-Germanic *frawītaną. By surface analysis, ver- + weisen.

adj:vierte.tx: From Middle High German vierde, from Old High German fiordo (akin to Old Saxon fiortho), from Proto-West Germanic *feurþō. Equivalent to vier + -te. Cognate with Dutch vierde, Danish fjerde, English fourth.

noun:Verlag.tx: From verlegen; used until the 16th century to mean “expenses”.

noun:Veilchen.tx: Diminutive of obsolete Vei(e)l, from Middle High German vīel, vīol, from Old High German fīol, from Latin viola. Doublet of Viole and Viola.

noun:Vetter.tx: From Middle High German veter, vetere, from Old High German fetiro (“father's brother”), fatureo, from Proto-West Germanic *faderjō or *fadurjō.

noun:Vieh.tx: From Middle High German vihe, from Old High German fihu, Proto-Germanic *fehu, from Proto-Indo-European *péḱu (“livestock, domestic animals”). Cognate with Low German Veeh, Dutch vee, English fee, Danish fæ.

noun:Viertel.tx: From Old High German fiorteil. Equivalent to vier + Teil.

noun:Volk.tx: From Middle High German volc, from Old High German folc, from Proto-West Germanic *folk, Proto-Germanic *fulką. Cognate with Dutch volk, English folk, Swedish folk, Norwegian Bokmål folk, Norwegian Nynorsk folk, Icelandic fólk and Danish folk. Doublet of Pulk.

adv:vielleicht.tx: From Middle High German vil līchte (“very easily”), thus: “what could easily happen”. Compare the same in German Low German villicht, Dutch wellicht, Saterland Frisian fielicht.

verb:verwunden.tx: From Middle High German verwunden, from Old High German [Term?], from Proto-West Germanic *frawundōn. The simplex was in use until Middle High German as wunden. Cognates include Dutch verwonden, English forwound, Old Saxon farwundon.

noun:Vesper.tx: From Middle High German vësper, from Old High German vëspera, from Latin vespera, from vesper. The alternative neuter gender in the sense “snack” is probably from the compound Vesperbrot.

noun:Vasall.tx: From Middle High German vassal, from Old French vassal.

noun:Vorhang.tx: From Middle High German vorhanc, vürhanc. By surface analysis, deverbal from vorhängen. Cognate with Dutch voorhang, Yiddish פֿירהאַנג (firhang).

adj:verloren.tx: From Middle High German verlorn, from Old High German firloran, from Proto-West Germanic *fraloʀan, from Proto-Germanic *fraluzanaz.

noun:Vegetarier.tx: From older Vegetarianer, a borrowing from English vegetarian.

noun:Vulkan.tx: Ultimately from Latin Vulcanus (“god of fire”). Attested as a mythological term in German since the 11th c. The modern sense since the 16th c. from an internationalism, whose precise development is uncertain; the earliest attestations of appellative use are found in Arabic بُرْكان (burkān, 13th c.), Old Spanish vulcan (13th c.), and Middle French vulcan (14th c.).

adj:verdächtig.tx: From Middle High German verdæhtic, ferdæhtic, equivalent to Verdacht + -ig. Cognate with Middle Low German vördachtich, vördechtich, German Low German verdächtig.

verb:vermuten.tx: From Middle Low German vormōden, composed of vor (“for”) + mōden (“to want, ask for”), piecewise equivalent to and synchronically analyzable as ver- + muten, from Mut + -en.

verb:verdunkeln.tx: From Middle High German vertunkeln, from Old High German firtunkalen. Equivalent to ver- + dunkeln.

verb:verbinden.tx: From Middle High German verbinden, from Old High German firbintan, from Proto-West Germanic *frabindan. Equivalent to ver- + binden. Cognate with Dutch verbinden and Old English forbindan (whence Middle English forbinden).

verb:vermelden.tx: From Middle High German vermëlden, from Old High German firmëldēn, firmëldōn, from Proto-West Germanic *framelþōn. Equivalent to ver- + melden.

verb:vollenden.tx: From Middle High German volenden (“to bring it to the complete ending”). Equivalent to voll- + enden.

verb:verzehren.tx: From Middle High German verzeren, verzern, vorzern, ferzeren, ferzern, forzern, from Old High German firzeran (“to tear up, consume”), from Proto-West Germanic *frateran (“to tear up, tear to shreds”), equivalent to ver- + zehren. Cognate with Middle Low German vörtēren (modern German Low German vertehren), Dutch verteren (“to consume, devour”), English fortear (“to tear up”).

verb:vermögen.tx: From Middle High German vermügen, vermugen, from Old High German firmugan, firmagan, from Proto-West Germanic *framagan. Equivalent to ver- + mögen.

verb:verstopfen.tx: From Middle High German verstophen, from Old High German firstopfōn, firstophōn, from Proto-West Germanic *frastoppōn; equivalent to ver- + stopfen. Cognate with Dutch verstoppen, English forstop.

noun:Vogelscheuche.tx: Compound of Vogel + Scheuche. See also German scheuchen

verb:verteidigen.tx: From Middle High German verteidingen, from vertagedingen, derived from teidinc, tagedinc (originally "judgment", then "talk, chatter", so Narrenteiding (“foolish chatter”)) of tac (“day”) and ding (“negotiation”). By surface analysis, ver- + Tag + Ding + -en. The term developed semantically from "court day with negotiations" > "to defend in court" > "to defend". Cognate with Dutch verdedigen.

noun:Verstand.tx: From Middle High German verstant, verstont, ferstant, from Old High German firstant (“intellect, wisdom”), from Proto-West Germanic *frastand, from Proto-West Germanic *frastandan (“to understand”), equivalent to ver- + Stand. Cognate with Middle Low German vörstant (whence German Low German Verstand), Dutch verstand. Related to verstehen.

noun:Vernunft.tx: From Middle High German vernunft, from Old High German vernumft. Verbal noun of vernehmen. The second part of the word is Middle High German numft, from Old High German numft, from Proto-West Germanic *numþi (“taking”).

noun:Vermögen.tx: From late Middle High German vermügen (“force, might”), an infinitive used as a noun, from Old High German furimugan, equivalent to modern ver- + mögen (“to like, want to”).

verb:versprechen.tx: From Middle High German versprechen (“to guarantee”), from Old High German firsprehhan (“to defend verbally, to warrant”), from Proto-West Germanic *frasprekan. Analyzable as ver- + sprechen. The sense “to misspeak” is a later transparent derivation (see the prefix).

verb:verfluchen.tx: From Middle High German vervluochen, from Old High German firfluohhan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraflōkan. Equivalent to ver- + fluchen.

noun:Verlust.tx: From Middle High German verlust, from Old High German farlust, from Proto-Germanic *fralustiz. Ultimately related to verlieren.

verb:verpfänden.tx: Derived from Pfand by means of prefix ver- and umlaut: ver- + pfänden.

verb:verschlingen.tx: From ver- + schlingen (“to swallow food without chewing”). Cognate with Dutch verslinden.

noun:Verkäufer.tx: From verkaufen + -er. Cognate with Dutch verkoper.

noun:Verkabelung.tx: From verkabeln (“to hook up with cables”) + -ung (“-ing”).

verb:verwirren.tx: From Middle High German verwirren, alteration (perhaps after the model of the unrelated irren (“to err, be lost”)) of older verwërren, from Old High German firwërran, a strong verb related with Old High German wërra (“controversy, complication”); compare English war. Analysable as ver- + wirr (“confused”) + -en, though the adjective is historically a backformation from the verb. Cognate with Dutch verwarren.

verb:verteilen.tx: From Middle High German verteilen, from Old High German farteilen, firteilen, from Proto-West Germanic *fradailijan, from Proto-Germanic *fradailijaną. Equivalent to ver- + teilen. Cognate with Dutch verdelen.

verb:verstecken.tx: From Middle High German verstecken, from Old High German firstekken. Equivalent to ver- + stecken. Cognate with Dutch versteken (“to hide”).

verb:verbergen.tx: From Middle High German verbergen, from Old High German firbergan, from Proto-West Germanic *frabergan. Equivalent to ver- + bergen. Compare Dutch verbergen, also Old English forbeorgan.

noun:Verdruss.tx: From Middle High German verdruʒ, from Old High German firthrôz, a verbal noun to firthriozan (“to chagrin”).

verb:verdrießen.tx: From Middle High German verdrieȥen, from Old High German firthrioȥan, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *firi- + *þreutaną (“to harass”). Akin to Middle Low German vordrêten (Danish fortryde), Middle Dutch verdrieten (Dutch verdrieten).

noun:Verbot.tx: From Old High German firbot, from Proto-Germanic *furibudą. Cognate with Dutch verbod, English forbode, Danish forbud, Swedish förbud.

noun:Vehemenz.tx: 17th century, from Latin vehementia, in part through French véhémence.

verb:versetzen.tx: From Middle High German versetzen, from Old High German firsezzen, from Proto-West Germanic *frasattjan. Equivalent to ver- + setzen. Compare Dutch verzetten, English forset.

noun:Versuch.tx: From Middle High German versuoch (“striving, undertaking, test, examination”), from Old High German firsuoh (“test, experiment”). See versuchen (“to try, attempt”).

verb:verschwören.tx: ver- + schwören, from Middle High German verswern, from Old High German firswerren, firswerien, farsweren, from Proto-West Germanic *fraswarjan. Cognate with Old Saxon farswerian, English forswear.

noun:Vielfraß.tx: From Middle High German vilvrāz, from Old High German filifrāz. By surface analysis, viel (“much”) + Fraß, the latter being used here in the now obsolete sense “eater” (rather than “food”).

noun:Verbesserung.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German vorbēteringe, since the 15th century. By surface analysis, verbessern + -ung.

verb:vorstellen.tx: From vor- + stellen. Compare Dutch voorstellen.

adj:verwitwet.tx: From Middle High German verwitewet, from Old High German firwituwēt. Originally the past participle of obsolete verwitwen. By surface analysis, ver- + Witwe + -t.

adj:vage.tx: Borrowed from French vague, from Latin vagus.

verb:verraten.tx: From Middle High German verrāten, from Old High German firrātan, from Proto-West Germanic *frarādan. Equivalent to ver- + raten. Cognate to Dutch verraden.

verb:verschmähen.tx: From Middle High German versmæhen, from Old High German firsmāhen, derived from Proto-West Germanic *smēhijan (“to sneer at, publicly despise”). Equivalent to ver- + schmähen (“to mock, verbally abuse”).

adj:verantwortlich.tx: ver- + Antwort (“answer”) + -lich, possibly inspired by Latin respondeō.

verb:verlegen.tx: From Middle High German verlegen (“to misplace, obstruct”), from Old High German firleggen (“to cover”). By surface analysis, ver- + legen.

adj:verlegen.tx: Older meaning “indecisive”, from Middle High German verlegen (“spoilt by idleness or flirtation”), from Old High German firlegan (“sluggish, adulterous”), from firliggen (“to commit adultery”).

verb:verzaubern.tx: From Middle High German verzoubern, from Old High German firzoubarōn. Equivalent to ver- + zaubern.

verb:verdenken.tx: From Middle High German verdenken, from Old High German firthenken, from Proto-West Germanic *fraþankijan. Equivalent to ver- + denken. Compare Dutch verdenken and Old English forþencan.

noun:Vieleck.tx: From viele (“many”) + Ecke (“corner”), likely a calque of Dutch veelhoek, coined by Simon Stevin as a purism for Latin polygōnum, from Ancient Greek πολύγωνον (polúgōnon).

verb:verschneiden.tx: From Middle High German versnīden, from Old High German firsnīdan. Equivalent to ver- + schneiden (“to cut”).

verb:versenken.tx: From Middle High German versenken, from Old High German firsenken. Equivalent to ver- + senken.

verb:vergeben.tx: From Middle High German vergëben, from Old High German fargëban, from Proto-Germanic *fragebaną. Analyzable as ver- + geben. Cognate with Dutch vergeven, English forgive, Icelandic fyrirgefa.

verb:verleiden.tx: From Middle High German verleiden, equivalent to ver- + leiden.

noun:Vorhaut.tx: From vor- (“fore-”) + Haut (“skin”), loosely after Latin praeputium. Chiefly spread by Luther (16th c.), but attested once or twice before him. The foreskin was of no special interest to the Germanic peoples and the need for a word arose only in biblical context. Translations were often ad-hoc formations or mere descriptions, though Überwachsung (literally “over-growth”) was somewhat common in the 15th century.

noun:Vielfalt.tx: From viel + -falt. Cognate with Middle English felefold, Dutch veelvoud. Compare Modern English manifold and manyfold.

verb:verführen.tx: From Middle High German vervüeren, from Old High German firfuoren. Equivalent to ver- + führen.

noun:Vorteil.tx: From Middle High German vorteil, voreteil, from Old High German forateila, equivalent to vor- (“before, better”) + Teil (“part, piece”). Compare English foredeal (“advantage, benefit”).

noun:Vorurteil.tx: From Middle High German vorurteile (“precedent”, ca. 1300), a calque of Latin praeiudicium. By surface analysis, vor- (“pre-”) + Urteil (“judgement”). The modern sense since the 16th century. Compare Dutch vooroordeel, Swedish fördom, etc.

noun:Ventil.tx: Borrowed from Medieval Latin ventīle, from Latin ventus (“wind”).

verb:vergewaltigen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German vergewaltigen, equivalent to ver- + gewaltig + -en.

adj:verständlich.tx: From Middle High German verstentlich, from Old High German firstantantlīh, from firstantan, from Proto-West Germanic *frastandan. Equivalent to verstehen + -lich. By surface analysis, Verstand + -lich.

noun:Völkermord.tx: From Völker + Mord. Occasional use from at least 1759; in the Napoleonic era popularised as a calque of the French revolutionary term populicide (1792). The German was calqued into English as folk-murdering by 1892. Both the French and the German may have influenced the younger genocide (1944).

verb:verlernen.tx: From Middle High German verlernen. Equivalent to ver- (indicating a faulty action) + lernen (“to learn”).

verb:verschieben.tx: From Middle High German verschieben, from Old High German firskioban. Equivalent to ver- + schieben.

noun:Verkauf.tx: From Middle High German verkouf, also attested as Old High German firkoufida. By surface analysis, deverbal from verkaufen.

verb:verkaufen.tx: From Middle High German verkoufen, from Old High German firkoufen. Equivalent to ver- + kaufen. Cognate with Dutch verkopen and Yiddish פֿאַרקויפֿן (farkoyfn).

adv:voraus.tx: From Middle High German vorūȥ, voreūȥ. By surface analysis, univerbation of vor + aus.

noun:Vertrag.tx: From late Middle High German vertraht, backformed from Middle High German vertragen (“convene, agree”). Compare Dutch verdrag.

verb:verletzen.tx: From Middle High German verletzen, ferletzen, equivalent to ver- + letzen.

noun:Verräter.tx: From Middle High German verrætere. Agent noun of verraten.

adj:vulgär.tx: Borrowed from French vulgaire, from Latin vulgāris.

noun:Völlerei.tx: From older Füllerei, ultimately from the root of voll (“full”).

verb:verschwinden.tx: From Middle High German verswinden, from Old High German firswintan, farswindan. Cognate with Middle Low German vorswinden, Dutch verzwinden. Equivalent to ver- + schwinden.

verb:versagen.tx: From Middle High German versagen, virsagen, vorsagen, fersagen, from Old High German firsagen, firsagēn (“to deny, refuse, excuse”), from Proto-West Germanic *frasaggjan, equivalent to ver- + sagen. Cognate with English forsay, Dutch verzeggen (“to deny, forbid”), German Low German verseggen (“to refuse, deny”), Swedish försäga (“to misspeak, say too much”).

verb:vergiften.tx: From Middle High German vergiften (“to give, donate, bequeath; to poison”), formally from Old High German firgiften (“to donate; to sell”). Analysable as ver- + Gift + -en or ver- + giften.

verb:vermieten.tx: From Middle High German vermieten, from Old High German firmieten. Equivalent to ver- + mieten.

noun:Velours.tx: Borrowed from French velours. Doublet of Flor.

noun:Vergissmeinnicht.tx: Univerbation of vergiss + mein + nicht, literally “forget me not”. The flower is considered a symbol of loyalty, friendship and remembrance. The verb vergessen used to be used with the object in the genitive case, using mein as the now-archaic genitive pronoun of ich. Therefore, the contemporary German construction would instead be "vergiss mich nicht".

noun:Visagist.tx: Borrowed from French visagiste, by surface analysis, Visage + -ist.

verb:verzweifeln.tx: From Middle High German verzwīveln (12th century), from Old High German firzwīvalen, firzwīfalen. By surface analysis, ver- + zweifeln (“to doubt”). Compare Dutch vertwijfelen, Swedish förtvivla, etc.

adj:vorhanden.tx: From vor den Händen (literally “in front of the hands”). Compare English to hand, at hand, on hand.

verb:vermissen.tx: From Middle High German vermissen, from Old High German firmissen. Equivalent to ver- + missen.

noun:Vorschlag.tx: From Middle High German vürslac. By surface analysis, deverbal from vorschlagen or vor- + Schlag. Compare the noun Vorschlagen, gerund of the verb vorschlagen, and Luxembourgish Virschlag.

noun:Verband.tx: Late 17th century, deverbal from verbinden, apparently after Dutch verband, from Middle Dutch verbant (ca. 1300), as several of the very earliest attestations are found in translations from Dutch (see citations page). Compare also Middle Low German vorbant (15th c.). By surface analysis, ver- + Band. Partially displaced older Verbund.

noun:Verfassung.tx: From Middle High German vervaʒʒunge; by surface analysis, verfassen + -ung.

verb:verwelken.tx: From Middle High German verwelken, ferwelken, equivalent to ver- + welken. Compare Middle Low German vörwelken, Old High German firswelkōn (“to wither”).

verb:verarmen.tx: From Middle High German verarmen, from Old High German firarmen, firermen. Equivalent to ver- + arm (“poor”) + -en.

noun:Verdacht.tx: From Middle High German verdâht from Middle High German verdenken (“to blame”). Cognate to the archaic Dutch noun verdacht.

verb:verbrennen.tx: From Middle High German verbrennen, from Old High German firbrinnan, from Proto-West Germanic *frabrinnan. Equivalent to ver- + brennen (“to burn”). Compare English forburn.

noun:Vorrat.tx: From Middle High German vorrāt. Equivalent to vor- (“before, in advance”) + Rat (“goods, effects” as in Hausrat).

verb:verlangen.tx: From Middle High German verlangen, equivalent to ver- + langen. Cognate with English forlong.

adv:vorwärts.tx: From vor- + -wärts; compare English forward and Dutch voorwaarts.

verb:verdammen.tx: From Middle High German verdampnen, from Old High German firdamnōn, from Proto-West Germanic *furidamnōn (“to damn, condemn”).

adj:väterlich.tx: From Middle High German veterlich, vaterlich, from Old High German faterlīh, from Proto-Germanic *fadurlīkaz, equivalent to Vater + -lich. Cognate with English fatherly, Dutch vaderlijk.

noun:Voreingenommenheit.tx: voreingenommen + -heit. Compare Dutch vooringenomenheid, Danish forudindtagethed.

verb:vermitteln.tx: From Middle High German vermitteln. By surface analysis, ver- + Mittel + -en.

verb:versehen.tx: From Middle High German versëhen, from Old High German firsëhan, from Proto-West Germanic *frasehwan. Equivalent to ver- + sehen. Cognate with Dutch verzien, Old English forsēon.

adj:versehen.tx: From Middle High German versëhen, from Old High German firsëhan, from Proto-West Germanic *frasehwan. Equivalent to ver- + sehen. Cognate with Dutch verzien, Old English forsēon.

verb:verdichten.tx: Derived from the adjective dicht (“dense”): ver- + dicht + -en

verb:versenden.tx: From Middle High German versenden, from Old High German firsenten. Equivalent to ver- + senden. Cognate with Dutch verzenden (“to send, to ship”).

verb:verhindern.tx: From Middle High German verhindern, from Old High German firhintaren. Equivalent to ver- + hindern.

verb:verjüngen.tx: ver- + jüngen, the second part being a now-obsolete standalone causative of jung (“young”).

verb:vereinbaren.tx: From Middle High German vereinbæren. Analyzable as ver- + ein + -bar + -en.

verb:verschwenden.tx: From Middle High German verswenden, from Old High German firswenten. A causative formation derived from German verschwinden (“to disappear”), Old High German firswintan (“to disappear”). Thus, the original meaning is "to make disappear".

verb:verscheiden.tx: From Middle High German verscheiden, from Old High German firskeidan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraskaiþan. Equivalent to ver- + scheiden. Cognates include Dutch verscheiden and Old English forsċeādan.

verb:vortragen.tx: From Middle High German vortragen, vürtragen, from Old High German furitragan, from Proto-West Germanic *foradragan. Equivalent to vor- + tragen. Compare Dutch voordragen, English foredraw, Swedish föredraga.

noun:Vertreter.tx: From Late Middle High German vertreter; vertreten + -er.

verb:vertreten.tx: From Middle High German vertrëten, from Old High German firtrëtan, from Proto-West Germanic *fratredan. By surface analysis, ver- + treten. Compare Dutch vertreden.

noun:Visier.tx: 15th century, from Middle French, from Old French visiere. The sense “sight” (late 16th century) under influence of related visieren, anvisieren (“to keep in view, aim at”).

verb:verwechseln.tx: From Middle High German verwëhseln, from Old High German firwëhsalen. Equivalent to ver- + wechseln.

adj:vorsichtig.tx: From vor- + Sicht + -ig. Compare Dutch voorzichtig, Yiddish פֿאָרזיכטיק (forzikhtik) and English foresighty.

adv:vorsichtig.tx: From vor- + Sicht + -ig. Compare Dutch voorzichtig, Yiddish פֿאָרזיכטיק (forzikhtik) and English foresighty.

verb:verbannen.tx: From Middle High German verbannen, from Old High German firbannan, from Proto-West Germanic *frabannan. Equivalent to ver- + bannen. Compare Dutch verbannen and English forban.

noun:Vergiftung.tx: Inherited from Middle High German vergiftunge (“poisoning”). Equivalent to vergiften + -ung.

noun:Verhör.tx: Deverbal from verhören; etymologically, from Late Middle High German [Term?].

verb:verhören.tx: From Middle High German verhœren. By surface analysis, ver- + hören.

noun:Vorwort.tx: Calque of Latin praefatio (“preface”), equivalent to vor + Wort or vor- + Wort.

verb:verderben.tx: From a merger of Middle High German verdërben (“to perish, die”) (a strong verb, descended from Old High German *fardërban, inherited from Proto-West Germanic *fraderban, which is in turn from Proto-Germanic *derbaną (“to perish”)) and of Middle High German verdẹrben (“bring ruin to, kill, damage”) (a weak verb, from a seeming Proto-West Germanic *fradarbijan); compare Middle Low German …

verb:verzeihen.tx: From Middle High German verzīhen, from Old High German firzīhan. Equivalent to ver- + zeihen.

adj:vielversprechend.tx: Literally, “much-promising”. From viel (“much”) + versprechend (present participle of versprechen (“to promise”)).

verb:verleiten.tx: From Middle High German verleiten, from Old High German firleiten, from Proto-West Germanic *fralaidijan. Equivalent to ver- + leiten. Cognate with Dutch verleiden, Old Saxon farlēdian, English forlead.

verb:verfahren.tx: From Middle High German vervarn, from Old High German firfaran, farfaran from Proto-Germanic *frafaraną, equivalent to ver- + fahren.

verb:verwaisen.tx: From Middle High German verweisen. By surface analysis, ver- + Waise (“orphan”) + -en.

adj:verpönt.tx: Past participle of earlier (18th century) verpönen (“to consider bad, to disapprove”), from earlier (15th century) verpēnen (“to punish with a fine”), from Middle High German pēn, pēne (“punishment”), from Medieval Latin pēna, from Classical Latin poena (“punishment, revenge, torment”).

verb:verunglimpfen.tx: 15th century, by surface analysis, ver- + Unglimpf + -en.

prep:voller.tx: Contraction of voll (“full”) + der (feminine and plural genitive article). This origin is not felt anymore, however, so the preposition can be used with masculine and neuter nouns just as well.

noun:Vorlage.tx: From Middle High German vorlāge. By surface analysis, deverbal from vorlegen.

noun:Vorsicht.tx: Chiefly a backformation from vorsichtig, from Middle High German vorsihtec, vürsihtec, from Old High German foresihtig, derived from foresiht, a calque of Latin providentia and provisio. By surface analysis, vor- + Sicht. Doublet of Vorsehung. Although the noun must underlie the adjective, the former is not attested again (after Notker) before the 15th century; it remained rare until ca. 1650. …

intj:Vorsicht.tx: Chiefly a backformation from vorsichtig, from Middle High German vorsihtec, vürsihtec, from Old High German foresihtig, derived from foresiht, a calque of Latin providentia and provisio. By surface analysis, vor- + Sicht. Doublet of Vorsehung. Although the noun must underlie the adjective, the former is not attested again (after Notker) before the 15th century; it remained rare until ca. 1650. …

verb:verrechnen.tx: From late Middle High German verrechenen (“to account for; to charge”), formally from Old High German firrehhanōn (“to recollect, remember”). Analysable as ver- + rechnen. Cognate with Dutch verrekenen.

adj:voluminös.tx: Borrowed from French volumineux. By surface analysis, Volumen + -ös.

noun:Volumen.tx: Learned borrowing from Latin volūmen (“scroll”). The sense of "capacity" is derived from French volume.

verb:vergehen.tx: From Middle High German vergān, vergāngēn, from Old High German firgān, from Proto-West Germanic *fragān. By surface analysis, ver- + gehen.

adj:vollkommen.tx: From Middle High German volkomen, volkumen, from Old High German folkoman. Equivalent to voll- + kommen.

adv:vollkommen.tx: From Middle High German volkomen, volkumen, from Old High German folkoman. Equivalent to voll- + kommen.

verb:verjagen.tx: From Middle High German verjagen, from Old High German firjagōn, from Proto-West Germanic *frajagōn. Equivalent to ver- + jagen.

noun:Verletzung.tx: From Middle High German verletzunge. Equivalent to verletzen + -ung.

noun:Verdienst.tx: From Middle High German verdienst. By surface analysis, ver- + Dienst. See dienen for more.

verb:verschweigen.tx: From Middle High German verswīgen, from Old High German firswīgēn. Equivalent to ver- + schweigen (“be silent”).

adj:variabel.tx: Borrowed from French variable, from Late Latin variabilis. By surface analysis, variieren (“to vary”) + -abel (“-able”).

verb:vertrauen.tx: From Middle High German vertrūwen, vertriuwen, from Old High German firtrūwēn, firtrūēn. Compare Alemannic German vertraue, Dutch vertrouwen, Low German vertruggen (Paderbornisch). By surface analysis, ver- + trauen.

verb:verwenden.tx: From Middle High German verwenden, ferwenden, from Old High German firwenten (“to turn away, avert, dissuade, hold back”), equivalent to ver- + wenden. Cognate with Middle Low German vörwenden, Low German verwenden.

noun:Vergebung.tx: Inherited from Middle High German vergëbunge (“pardon; poisoning”). Equivalent to vergeben + -ung.

verb:verdauen.tx: From Middle High German verdouwen, verdöuwen, from Old High German firthouwen, firdouwen, firthewen, firdewen. Equivalent to ver- + tauen (“to thaw”), thus originally "to make melt away".

noun:Völkerball.tx: Equivalent to Völker (“peoples, nations”) + Ball (“ball”), from the idea that it represents a war between two countries, the “out” players being the fallen.

verb:verbreiten.tx: ver- + breit (“broad”) + -en; cognate with Luxembourgish verbreeden

verb:versuchen.tx: From ver- + suchen. Compare English forseek, Dutch verzoeken.

verb:versichern.tx: From Middle High German versichern. Equivalen to ver- + sichern. The insurance sense (17th c.) is a calque of Italian assicurare.

verb:vererben.tx: From Middle High German [Term?]; ver- + erben.

verb:vermasseln.tx: Derived around 1900 from ver- + Massel (“luck”), a loan from Yiddish מזל (mazel, “luck, destiny”), from Medieval Hebrew מַזָּל (mazzāl).

noun:Vorjahr.tx: From vor- (“before”) + Jahr (“year”). Compare Dutch voorjaar (“spring”).

verb:versöhnen.tx: From Middle High German versüenen, versuonen, from Old High German firsuonen, from the same root as Sühne. The change of the root vowel from ü to ö is probably due to Low German influence, compare Middle Low German vorsȫnen, versoenen.

verb:vergelten.tx: From Middle High German vergëlten, from Old High German firgëltan, from Proto-West Germanic *frageldan, from Proto-Germanic *frageldaną, equivalent to ver- + gelten (“to be worth”). Cognate with English foryield, Dutch vergelden.

verb:verfügen.tx: From Middle High German vervüegen, ferfüegen, equivalent to ver- + fügen. Cognate with German Low German verfögen, Dutch vervoegen, Danish forføje, Swedish förfoga.

verb:verabreichen.tx: From now-obsolete abreichen (“to give, offer”) (compare abgeben), with emphatic ver-.

pt: to follow, chase, dog, hound, haunt, persecute, pursue, shadow, track
noun:Verfolger.tx: From verfolgen (“to follow, chase, dog, hound, haunt, persecute, pursue, shadow, track”) + -er.

noun:Vibrato.tx: Borrowed from Italian vibrato, the past participle of vibrare.

verb:verpflichten.tx: From Middle High German verphlichten. Cognate with Dutch verplichten. Equivalent to ver- + pflichten. Also analysable as ver- + Pflicht (“duty”) + -en.

noun:Vorbau.tx: From Middle High German vorbū, vorebū. Equivalent to vor- + Bau.

adj:vermeintlich.tx: vermeinen (“think, believe, suspect, suppose”) + -t- + -lich. Related to meinen.

verb:verlaufen.tx: From Middle High German verloufen, from Old High German firloufan (“to pass, overtake”). By surface analysis, ver- + laufen. Cognate with Dutch verlopen.

verb:vergeuden.tx: From Middle High German vergiuden, from ver- + giuden, further etymology unknown.

noun:Versuchung.tx: From Middle High German versuochunge. By surface analysis, versuchen + -ung.

verb:verkünden.tx: From Middle High German verkünden, from Old High German farkunden, from Proto-West Germanic *frakunþijan. Cognate with Old English forcȳþan, also related to Dutch verkondigen.

verb:vorgeben.tx: Equivalent to vor- + geben, see also Middle Low German vȫrgēven (“pretend”), English foregive, and Danish foregive (“pretend”).

verb:vernichten.tx: From Middle High German vernihten, from nihten, from niht. By surface analysis, ver- + nicht + -en.

noun:Vorbild.tx: From Middle High German vorbilde, from Old High German forabilidi. Equivalent to vor + Bild. Cognate to Dutch voorbeeld.

verb:vergraulen.tx: 20th century, from ver- + graulen (“to be scared”, rare or regional). The latter is from earlier graueln, a variant of (also rare) gräueln, from Middle High German griuweln, grūweln, whence the noun Gräuel (“horror”). The form with -ūw- (modern -au-) probably shows the same Central German development as in brauen, kauen. The change from -eln to -len is unremarkable (in fact, many speakers merge these entirely).

adj:vorstellbar.tx: Derived from the verb vorstellen: vorstell- (“imagine”) + -bar (“-able”).

adj:verrußt.tx: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

verb:vergolden.tx: From Middle High German vergolden, variant (with readaptation to the noun) of vergulden. Analysable as ver- + Gold + -en. Cognate with Dutch vergulden.

verb:verladen.tx: From Middle High German verladen, from Old High German firladan. Equivalent to ver- + laden.

noun:Vaterland.tx: From Middle High German vaterlant, from Old High German faterlant, constructed as Vater + Land, following Latin patria.

noun:Verhütung.tx: verhüten + -ung. In the sense of “contraception” short for Empfängnisverhütung.

verb:vorkommen.tx: From Middle High German vorekomen, forekomen, vurekomen, vürekomen, from Old High German furaqueman, furakweman, furiqueman, furikweman, from Proto-West Germanic *forakweman, from Proto-Germanic *furaikwemaną, equivalent to vor- + kommen. Cognate with English forecome.

verb:vertragen.tx: From Middle High German vertragen, from Old High German firtragan, fartragan, from Proto-Germanic *fradraganą, equal to ver- + tragen. Cognate with Middle Low German verdragen, Dutch verdragen.

noun:Versiegelung.tx: From the verb versiegeln (to seal), from siegeln, from the noun Siegel (seal) + the noun suffix -ung

verb:verzichten.tx: 18th century, denominal from Verzicht + -en, displacing related sich (einer Sache) verzeihen. The significantly earlier attestation of Middle Low German vortichten, Middle Dutch vertichten (15th c.) makes it likely that the High German formation is based on these.

noun:Vuvuzela.tx: From Zulu vuvuzela, likely through English. Popularised before and during the 2010 World Cup and still chiefly associated with that tournament.

adj:verkäuflich.tx: From Middle High German *verkouflich, from Old High German firkouflīh. By surface analysis, verkaufen + lich.

verb:verhehlen.tx: From Middle High German verheln, from Old High German firhelan, from Proto-Germanic *frahelaną. By surface analysis, ver- + hehlen.

verb:verbrauchen.tx: ver- + brauchen. Cognate to Dutch verbruiken.

noun:Vorbedingung.tx: From Middle High German vorbedingunge. Equivalent to vor + Bedingung.

verb:verstreichen.tx: From Middle High German verstrīchen, from Old High German firstrīhhan. Equivalent to ver- + streichen.

verb:verwandeln.tx: From Middle High German verwandelen, ferwandelen, from Old High German firwantalōn, from Proto-Germanic *frawandlōną, equivalent to ver- + wandeln. Cognate with Low German verwanneln, Saterland Frisian ferwondelje.

adj:vermisst.tx: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

noun:V-Mann.tx: Clipping of Verbindungsmann or Vertrauensmann, from Verbindung (“connection”) + Mann (“man”).

verb:versinken.tx: From Middle High German versinken, from Old High German firsinkan, firsincan. Equivalent to ver- + sinken.

noun:Vagabund.tx: From French vagabond, from Late Latin vagābundus. Compare Latin vagari, from vagus.

noun:Verleihung.tx: The two senses are from the corresponding senses of verleih(en) ("award, confer") + ung (a nominalising suffix)

noun:Vestibül.tx: Borrowed from French vestibule, from Latin vestibulum.

adv:vielerorts.tx: From vieler + Ort + -s (adverbial suffix); compare allerorts, mancherorts.

noun:Versuchsballon.tx: From Versuch (“trial”) + -s- + Ballon (“balloon”), calque of French ballon d'essai.

verb:verirren.tx: From Middle High German verirren, from Old High German firirrо̄n, from Proto-West Germanic *farirʀijōn. Equivalent to ver- + irren.

noun:Vergnügung.tx: From vergenügen + -ung , from Middle High German vergenüegen (zufriedenstellen), derived from genug.

adj:verlogen.tx: Originally the past participle of the obsolete verb verlügen, from Middle High German verlogen, from Old High German firlogan.

noun:Viadukt.tx: Latin via + ductus, past participle of duco

verb:vertun.tx: From Middle High German vertuon, from Old High German fartuon, firtuon (“to fordo, waste, destroy”), from Proto-West Germanic *fradōn, from Proto-Germanic *fardōną, *fradōną (“to ruin, destroy”). Equivalent to ver- + tun. Cognate with English fordo, Dutch verdoen.

verb:verrotten.tx: From Middle Low German vorrotten, a compounding of vor- and rotten.

verb:verleumden.tx: From Middle High German verliumden, contracted form of verliumunden. Equivalent to Leumund + ver- -en.

verb:versäumen.tx: From Middle High German versūmen, from Old High German firsūmen. By surface analysis, ver- + säumen. Compare Dutch verzuimen, Danish forsømme.

verb:verschränken.tx: From Middle High German verschrenken, from Old High German firskrenken. Equivalent to ver- + schränken.

noun:Vogt.tx: From Middle High German voget, from Old High German fogat, borrowed from Late Latin vocātus, from Classical Latin advocātus. Doublet of Advokat.

verb:verloben.tx: From Middle High German verloben, synchronically analyzable as ver- + loben. Cognate with Low German ferluawen, as well as Norwegian Bokmål forlove and Dutch verloven.

adj:virtuos.tx: Borrowed from Italian virtuoso, from Latin virtuōsus.

noun:Vaterschaft.tx: From Middle High German vaterschaft, faterschaft, equivalent to Vater (“father”) + -schaft (“-ship, -hood”). Compare English fathership.

verb:vorsehen.tx: From Middle High German vorsëhen, from Old High German forasëhan, from Proto-West Germanic *forēsehwan. Equivalent to vor- + sehen. Cognate with Dutch voorzien, English foresee (from Old English foresēon).

verb:vertreiben.tx: From Middle High German vertrīben, from Old High German firtrīban, from Proto-West Germanic *fradrīban. By surface analysis, ver- + treiben. Cognate with Old English fordrīfan, Old Saxon fardrīvan, English fordrive, Dutch verdrijven.

verb:verwittern.tx: ver- + wittern, from Middle High German witeren, from Middle High German weter, from Old High German wetar. From Proto-Germanic *wedrą (“weather”), eventually from Proto-Indo-European *wedʰrom.

verb:vernehmen.tx: From Middle High German vernëmen, from Old High German firnëman, from Proto-West Germanic *franeman, from Proto-Germanic *franemaną (“to take away”), equivalent to ver- + nehmen.

verb:vermischen.tx: From Middle High German vermischen, from Old High German firmisken, equivalent to ver- (“for-”) + mischen (“to mix”). Compare Old High German firmiskilǒn (“to mix up”).

verb:verfehlen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German vervælen. Equivalent to ver- + fehlen.

noun:Verlass.tx: From Middle High German verlāz (“inheritance; inaction”), from the same root as verlassen. The sense of reliance is a calque of Middle Low German verlāt.

noun:Vorfahre.tx: From Middle High German vorvar, from vorvaren (“to go ahead, to precede”).

verb:verspielen.tx: From Middle High German verspiln. Analyzable as ver- + spielen. In the sense of “to squander” reinforced by and merged with unrelated Middle Low German verspillen, verspilden (“to waste”). Compare Dutch verspillen.

noun:Vorsitzender.tx: Nominalization of vorsitzend, most likely a calque of Latin praeses. Attested since the 17th century, according to Google Books analysis.

verb:verbittern.tx: From Middle High German verbittern. Equivalent to ver- + bitter + -en.

verb:verbleichen.tx: From Middle High German verblīchen, from Old High German firblīhhan. Equivalent to ver- + bleichen.

verb:verklagen.tx: From Middle High German verklagen (“to accuse”), from Old High German firklagōn (“to bemoan, lament”). Equivalent to ver- + klagen.

noun:Verdrängung.tx: Coined by Johann Friedrich Herbart in 1824 and popularized by Sigmund Freud.

pron:vieles.tx: Neuter singular form of viel (“much, many”).

noun:Verschleiß.tx: From verschlissen, from ver- + schleißen (“to wear out, to tear”) (see there for more).

noun:Verbund.tx: Middle High German verbunt, in the technical senses newly formed from verbinden.

verb:vorbehalten.tx: From Middle High German vorbehalten. Equivalent to vor- + behalten.

noun:Verzicht.tx: From Middle High German verziht, from ver- + a derivative of zeihen (“to accuse, blame”) (DWDS).

verb:verhungern.tx: From Middle High German verhungern, equivalent to ver- + hungern.

verb:verabreden.tx: ver- + abreden, the latter from ab- + reden.

verb:veräppeln.tx: Unknown. First appeared at the start of the 20th century in central and northern Germany. Pertaining to Appel (“apple”), a Central and Low German form of standard Apfel. The motivation is unclear and possibly secondary. Perhaps derived from Middle Low German āpen (“to tease”), from āpe (“ape, monkey”).

noun:Vorgabe.tx: Deverbal from vorgeben. Also analysable as vor- + Gabe.

noun:Vorzeichen.tx: In the sense “omen” from Middle High German vorzeichen, from Old High German forazeihhan, from Proto-Germanic *furaitaikną. Cognate with Old English foretācen (English foretoken). In the technical senses simply from vor- (“before, in front”) + Zeichen (“sign”).

verb:verbleiben.tx: From Middle High German verblīben, verlīben. Equivalent to ver- + bleiben.

verb:verziehen.tx: From Middle High German verziehen, from Old High German farziohan, from Proto-West Germanic *frateuhan. By surface analysis, ver- + ziehen.

adj:vorletzte.tx: By surface analysis, vor- (“fore-, pre-”) + letzte (“last”).

verb:verantworten.tx: From Middle High German verantwürten, verantworten, equivalent to ver- + antworten. Cognate of Yiddish פֿאַרענטפֿערן (farentfern), Dutch verantwoorden, Afrikaans verantwoord, Luxembourgish veräntweren, West Frisian ferantwurdzje, Saterland Frisian feroantwoudje and Middle Low German vorantworden.

verb:verfangen.tx: From Middle High German vervāhen, from Old High German firfāhan. Equivalent to ver- + fangen; see the latter for the phonetic development.

verb:verfallen.tx: From Middle High German vervallen, from Old High German firfallan, from Proto-West Germanic *frafallan. Equivalent to ver- + fallen.

verb:vertagen.tx: From Middle High German vertagen. Equivalent to Tag (“day”) + ver- -en

verb:verwehren.tx: From Middle High German verwern, from Old High German firwerren, firwerien. Equivalent to ver- + wehren.

verb:verwundern.tx: Inherited from Middle High German verwundern. Equivalent to ver- + wundern.

verb:vollziehen.tx: From Middle High German volleziehen, from Old High German follaziohan; by surface analysis, voll- + ziehen. Compare Dutch voltrekken.

noun:Vergabe.tx: Deverbal from vergeben. Also analysable as ver- + Gabe.

noun:Vernehmung.tx: From Middle High German vernemung; vernehmen + -ung.

noun:Verschärfung.tx: verschärfen + -ung; see Danish skærpe and skærpelse for a similar metaphor.

noun:Vertreibung.tx: From Middle High German vertrībunge, from Old High German firtrībunga. By surface analysis, vertreiben + -ung.

verb:verwerten.tx: Formally from Middle High German verwerten (“to get old, frail; to decay”), from Old High German firwerten (“to ruin, decay, infamize”). The modern sense came about in the 19th century. Equivalent to ver- + werten.

noun:Vorzug.tx: Nominal formation derived from vorziehen (“to prefer, favor”).

adj:verworfen.tx: From Middle High German verworfen, from Old High German firworfan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraworpan, from Proto-Germanic *frawurpanaz.

verb:verwerfen.tx: From Middle High German verwërfen, from Old High German firwërfan, from Proto-West Germanic *frawerpan, from Proto-Germanic *frawerpaną. Equivalent to ver- + werfen.

phrase:vier Augen sehen mehr als zwei.tx: Literally, “four eyes see more than two”.

adj:verschollen.tx: From an obsolete participle of verschallen.

verb:verbeißen.tx: From Middle High German verbeizen, from Old High German *firbītan, from Proto-West Germanic *frabītan. Equivalent to ver- + beißen. Cognates include Dutch verbijten and English forbite.

verb:verwahrlosen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German verwarlōsen (from which was borrowed Dutch verwaarlozen), synchronically analyzed as ver- (“for-”) + Old High German wara (“attention”) + -los (“-less”) + -en (“verbal suffix”).

noun:Verschwörungstheoretiker.tx: Verschwörung (“conspiracy”) + -s- (“genitival interfix”) + Theoretiker (“theorist”), calque of English conspiracy theorist.

verb:verschlafen.tx: From Middle High German verslāfen, from Old High German firslāfan, equivalent to ver- + schlafen.

adv:vollends.tx: From Middle High German vollen, alternative form of Middle High German vol, with an unetymological -d- and suffixed with adverbial -s. Possibly influenced by vollenden, but not directly related to it.

verb:verneinen.tx: From Middle High German verneinen, from Old High German firneinen. By surface analysis, ver- + nein + -en.

verb:verstümmeln.tx: From Middle High German verstümbeln, verstumeln. By surface analysis, ver- + Stummel (“stump”) + -en.

noun:Vorrede.tx: From Middle High German vorrede, vorred, probably a calque of Latin praefātiō, praelocūtiō. Analysable as vor + Rede. Cognate to Middle Low German Vörrede (Vörrëde).

noun:Verdeck.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German vordecke (“deck of a ship”).

noun:Vorschlaghammer.tx: From vorschlagen (“to strike first”) + Hammer (“hammer”). It seems originally to have meant a smaller hammer used by the foreman to indicate the places where the other men must hit. The modern sense may be from confusion with (1.) Low German Vörhamer (Middle Low German vȫrehāmer, cf. English forehammer), meaning a heavy hammer used for the initial rough work, and (2.) Schlaghammer, also referring …

verb:verzetteln.tx: Frequentative of Middle High German verzetten (“to scatter, disperse”), from ver- + Old High German zetten (“to spread”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tadjaną (“to strew, scatter”). Combination of zetten with the instrumental suffix -eln yielded the cognate noun Zettel (“warp”); its etymologically unrelated homonym meaning “slip/piece of paper, note” in turn feeds into sense 1 of verzetteln by …

verb:verwehen.tx: From Middle High German verwæjen, from Old High German firwāen. Equivalent to ver- + wehen.

noun:Viech.tx: Doublet of Vieh from Upper German. Hence from Middle High German vihe, from Old High German fihu, from Proto-Germanic *fehu, from Proto-Indo-European *peḱu- (“livestock, domestic animals”).

noun:Vormund.tx: From Middle High German vormunde, from Old High German foramunto, a compound of fora (“before, in front of”, whence German vor) + munt (“hand; protection; guardianship”), the latter from Proto-Germanic *mundō. In contemporary understanding it is usually reanalysed as vor + Mund (“mouth”, unrelated with the former word), thus “who speaks for someone before they can speak for themselves”; thence …

noun:Verderben.tx: See verderben (“to spoil, rob, cause to perish”)

verb:verlocken.tx: Middle High German verlocken, from Old High German firlokkōn, corresponding to ver- + locken.

noun:Vertiefung.tx: From vertiefen + -ung. Compare Dutch verdieping, Swedish fördjupning, Middle Low German vördēpinge.

verb:verfassen.tx: From Middle High German verfaȥȥen, equivalent to ver- (“for-”) + fassen (“to grasp, seize”), perhaps formed after the model of the unrelated Latin concipiō (“to devise, conceive”) and its respective components.

verb:verneigen.tx: From Middle High German verneigen. By surface analysis, ver- + neigen.

verb:vertuschen.tx: From Middle High German vertuschen, vertussen, vertuzzen (“to cover up, hide”), from tuschen (“to keep quiet, hide something”), further origin obscure. Apparently related to Middle Low German vörtussen (“to hide, cover up, suppress”). Compare also Old High German firtuskōn (“to confuse, mislead”). Influenced in meaning by false association with unrelated tuschen (“to paint, use mascara”).

verb:verwesen.tx: From Middle High German verwësen, Old High German *firwësan (“to come to nothing, pass away, destroy”). Cognate with Old Norse visinn (“faded, decayed”), Old English weornian (“to destroy”), Gothic 𐍆𐍂𐌰𐍅𐌹𐍃𐌰𐌽 (frawisan, “to consume, waste, squander”). Compare Latin virus, Ancient Greek ἰός (iós), Sanskrit विष (viṣa, “poison”).

noun:Vokuhila.tx: Syllabic abbreviation of vorne kurz, hinten lang (“front short, back long”).

verb:verwöhnen.tx: From Middle High German verwenen, vorwenen, ferwenen, equivalent to ver- + wöhnen. Cognate with German Low German verwennen, Dutch verwennen.

adj:verschroben.tx: From the obsolete past participle of verschrauben (“to (mis-)screw”).

noun:Vorsatz.tx: vor- (“pre-”) + Satz (“sentence”). Possibly a calque of Latin prōpositum.

verb:verblüffen.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German verbluffen. Compare Dutch verbluffen.

noun:Vlies.tx: 16th century, at first only in reference to the Order of the Golden Fleece, from Middle Dutch vlies, from Proto-West Germanic *fleus. The later freer use for “fleece” was reinforced by inherited Low German forms, whereas the rare Middle High German vlius had no continuation. The spelling with V- follows the Dutch, but was supported by an unetymological association with Latin vellus. Doublet of …

adj:verhandelbar.tx: From verhandeln + -bar. Cognate with Dutch verhandelbaar.

noun:Verschluss.tx: From verschließen (“to close; to shut; to lock”).

verb:veröden.tx: From Middle High German verœden, from Old High German firо̄den, from Proto-West Germanic *farauþjan. Equivalent to ver- + öden. Related to öde.

verb:verhöhnen.tx: From Middle High German verhœnen. By surface analysis, ver- + höhnen.

verb:verrühren.tx: From Middle High German verrüeren, ferrüeren, equivalent to ver- + rühren.

noun:Vaterunser.tx: Univerbation of the prayer’s first two words Vater unser: From Middle High German vatir unsir etc., from Old High German fater unser, translation of Latin Pater noster, itself translated from Ancient Greek πάτερ ἡμῶν (páter hēmôn). The postposition of the possessive was still grammatical in Old High German and early Middle High German, but has survived to this day under continuous backing of the …

verb:vertauschen.tx: From Middle High German vertūschen, fertūschen, equivalent to ver- + tauschen.

verb:verschlucken.tx: From ver- + schlucken (“to swallow”). In “to swallow up”, the prefix is used in the sense of “entirely, completely”. In “to choke”, it is used in the sense of “wrongly, faultily” (equivalent to English *to mis-swallow).

verb:vernebeln.tx: From Middle High German nëbelen, nibelen, from Old High German nibulen. Equivalent to ver- + Nebel + -n.

adj:verquer.tx: Küpper supposes a univerbation of für (“for”) + quer (“crosswise”), the first part being matched to ver-. Attestations as an adverb reach as far back as the 16th century. Use as an adjective dates at least to the 18th century.

verb:verdorren.tx: From Middle High German verdorren, from Old High German firdorrēn. Equivalent to ver- + dorren.

adj:vertan.tx: From Middle High German vertān, from Old High German firtān.

pt: law (system of formal statutes and informal normative principles)
noun:Vertragsrecht.tx: From Vertrag (“contract”) + -s- + Recht (“law (system of formal statutes and informal normative principles)”).

adj:verdutzt.tx: 18th century, from Low German verduttet, participle of Middle Low German vordutten (“to confuse, madden”). Cognate with Icelandic dotta (“to nod off”). The form with -tz- may be a mechanical adaptation to the Standard German consonantism or alternatively a derivation with the intensive suffix -sen.

verb:verkühlen.tx: Widespread dialectal form, from ver- + kühl + -en. Compare Low German verköhlen, Yiddish פֿאַרקילן (farkiln).

adj:vorvorletzte.tx: From vor- (“fore-, pre-”) + vorletzte (“second to last”). By surface analysis, vor- + vor- + letzte, literally “pre-pre-last”.

verb:verschulden.tx: From Middle High German verschulden, from Old High German firskulden (“be guilty of, forfeit”). Equivalent to ver- + schulden.

verb:verfälschen.tx: From Middle High German vörvelschen, vorvelschen, from Old High German *farfalskōn, from Proto-West Germanic *frafalskōn. Equivalent to ver- + fälschen.

adj:vaterlos.tx: From Middle High German vaterlōs, faterlōs, from Old High German faterlōs, from Proto-Germanic *fadērlausaz, equivalent to Vater + -los. Cognate with English fatherless.

adj:verfassungsrechtlich.tx: From Verfassungsrecht + -lich. By surface analysis, Verfassung + -s- + rechtlich.

adj:verhasst.tx: From Middle High German verhazzet, from Old High German firhazzēt.

adj:verlustig.tx: Middle High German verlustec, corresponding to Verlust + -ig

adj:verrucht.tx: From Middle High German verruochet, participle of Middle High German verruochen (“to stop caring about something”), compound of ruochen (“to care”), from Proto-Germanic *rōkijaną (“to care, take care”). Related to geruhen (“to deign, condescend”) and ruchlos (“reckless”).

verb:verschlagen.tx: From Middle High German verslahen, from Old High German firslahan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraslahan. By surface analysis, ver- + schlagen. Cognate with Old English forslēan and Dutch verslaan.

adj:verschlagen.tx: From Middle High German verslagen, from Old High German firslagan, from Proto-West Germanic *fraslagan.

adj:versonnen.tx: Participle of obsolete sich versinnen (“to lose oneself in thought”). Further etymology at sinnen.

adj:verstohlen.tx: Originally the past participle of the obsolete verb verstehlen, from Middle High German verstoln, from Old High German *firstolan (attested as firstolano).

adj:verworren.tx: From the verb verwirren, diachronically from the participle of verwërren.

adj:vorder.tx: From Middle High German vorder, from Old High German fordarōn. Compare English further and thus farther.

noun:Vordermann.tx: From vorder (“front”) + Mann (“man; male human being”).

pt: Saint Vitus, who was assumed to be the patron of those affected
noun:Veitstanz.tx: From Veit (“Saint Vitus, who was assumed to be the patron of those affected”) + -s- + Tanz (“dance”).

verb:verprassen.tx: From ver- + prassen. Compare Dutch verbrassen.

verb:vorfinden.tx: From vor- + finden. Compare German Low German vörfinden, vörfinnen, Dutch voorvinden, Saterland Frisian foarfiende.

verb:vorenthalten.tx: From Middle High German vorenthalten, equivalent to vor- + enthalten.

verb:verleugnen.tx: From Middle High German verlougenen, verlougen, from Old High German firlougnen, firlougen, firlouganen. Equivalent to ver- + leugnen.

noun:Verlaub.tx: Derived from verlauben (probably on the model of Middle Low German verlōf), a northern variant of erlauben. Compare Dutch verlof, whence also English furlough.

verb:versaufen.tx: From Middle High German versūfen, from Old High German firsūfan. Equivalent to ver- + saufen.

verb:verpetzen.tx: ver- + petzen, since the end of the 18th century.

verb:vollbringen.tx: From Middle High German volbringen, from Old High German folbringan, follabringan. Equivalent to voll- + bringen. Cognate with Dutch volbrengen, English fullbring.

verb:verhauen.tx: From Middle High German verhouwen, from Old High German firhouwan. Equivalent to ver- + hauen.

verb:verharren.tx: From Middle High German verharren (“to stay, linger”), equivalent to ver- + harren. Cognate with Middle Low German vörharren (“to remain, stay, hold out, endure, wait”), Middle Dutch verharren (“to be or become too firm”).

verb:verpfeifen.tx: From ver- + pfeifen. The sense "piss off" seems to be a euphemism for verpissen.

verb:verkommen.tx: From Middle High German verkomen, from Old High German *firkweman, from Proto-West Germanic *frakweman, from Proto-Germanic *frakwemaną. Equivalent to ver- + kommen.

verb:vorsagen.tx: From vor- + sagen. Compare Dutch voorzeggen.

verb:verklemmen.tx: From Middle High German verklemmen, ferklemmen, equivalent to ver- + klemmen. Cognate with Middle English forclemmen.

verb:verfechten.tx: From Middle High German verfehten, from Old High German firfechtan. Equivalent to ver- + fechten.

verb:verhärten.tx: From Middle High German verherten, from Old High German firherten. Equivalent to ver- + härten.

verb:verheeren.tx: From Middle High German verhern, from Old High German farheriōn, originally "to defeat with an army," equivalent to ver- + the root of Heer (“army”).

verb:verschießen.tx: From Middle High German verschieȥen, from Old High German firskioȥan. Equivalent to ver- + schießen.

verb:verwirken.tx: From Middle High German verwirken, verwürken, from Old High German firwirken, firwurken, from Proto-West Germanic *frawurkijan, from Proto-Germanic *frawurkijaną. Equivalent to ver- + wirken.

verb:vertilgen.tx: From Middle High German vertilgen, vertiligen, from Old High German firtīligōn. Equivalent to ver- + tilgen.

verb:verkehren.tx: From Middle High German verkēren. Equivalent to ver- + kehren. Compare Yiddish פֿאַרקערן (farkern) and Afrikaans verkeer.

verb:verschaukeln.tx: ver- + schaukeln. Compare schummeln for the meaning, or English to wind up.

verb:verwinden.tx: From Middle High German verwinden, from Old High German firwintan. Equivalent to ver- + winden.

verb:verschmachten.tx: From northern Middle High German versmahten. By surface analysis, ver- + schmachten.

verb:vergießen.tx: From Middle High German vergiezen, from Old High German firgioȥan. Equivalent to ver- + gießen.

verb:verwahren.tx: From Middle High German verwarn. Equivalent to ver- + wahren.

verb:vollmachen.tx: voll- (“full, fully”) + machen (“to make”), literally “to fully-make; to make full”

phrase:von hinten Lyzeum, von vorne Muse.tx: Literally, “from behind [like] grammar school, from the front [like] museum”, that is, her dressing younger fails her as soon as one sees her face. Compare the same saying in some other continental European languages. The word Lyzeum (“grammar school for girls”) is now not used anymore, for which reason the saying has also become dated.

verb:verebben.tx: From Old High German firebban. Equivalent to ver- + ebben.

phrase:vom Regen in die Traufe.tx: Literally, “from the rain into the eaves”, referring to the situation where someone runs from the rain towards a house and is hit by a gush of water running down the roof, thereby becoming wetter than they could have become in normal rain.

verb:vergewissern.tx: From Middle High German vergewissern (“to provide a guarantee”), synchronically analyzed as ver- + gewiss + -ern.

verb:verrecken.tx: From Middle High German verrecken, from Old High German firrekken. Equivalent to ver- + recken.

verb:verhunzen.tx: From hunzen (“treat like a dog”), from Hund (“dog”).

verb:vereiteln.tx: Formally continuing Middle High German verītelen (“to become weak, insipid”, a 14th-c. hapax). By surface analysis, eitel (“vain”) + ver- -en. In Early Modern German, it is attested for “to empty, deplete”. The contemporary sense has been in use since the 18th c. While it can easily be explained from the underlying adjective, it should be noted that the same sense was well established in Middle …

noun:Vielweiberei.tx: viel (“many”) + Weib (“woman”) (archaic) + -erei, loosely calquing Ancient Greek πολυγαμία (polugamía, “polygamy”). First attested in the 17th century.

verb:verdünnisieren.tx: Ca. 1900, from ver- + dünn (“thin”) + -isieren (“-ize”), humorously for older sich dünn machen (literally “to make oneself thin”).

verb:versiegeln.tx: From Middle High German versigelen, from Old High German firsigilen. Equivalent to ver- + siegeln.

verb:verkorksen.tx: First attested in the late 19th century. Originally in the phrase sich den Magen verkorksen (“to upset one’s stomach”), from dialectal gorksen, gurgsen (“to make a gargling sound”). Related with gurgeln (“to gargle”). The form with k apparently by folk-etymological adaptation to Kork (“cork”), perhaps associated with how cork may ruin wine.

noun:Vorwitz.tx: From Old High German firiwizzi. Compare Swedish förvett, Danish forvid, Old English firwitt.

noun:Versucher.tx: From Middle High German versuocher. By surface analysis, versuchen + er.

noun:Vorsehung.tx: From Late Middle High German fürsehung (15th c.), a calque of Latin providentia and provisio. By surface analysis, vorsehen + -ung. Doublet of Vorsicht.

noun:Verzug.tx: From Middle High German verzuc, verzoc.

verb:verwachsen.tx: From ver- + wachsen. Compare archaic Dutch verwassen.

verb:veruntreuen.tx: From Middle High German veruntriuwen, from Old High German firuntriuwēn. Equivalent untreu + ver- -en.

verb:versiegen.tx: From the past participle of verseihen.

verb:vergnügen.tx: From Middle High German vergenüegen (zufriedenstellen), derived from genug.

noun:Veld.tx: Borrowed from Afrikaans veld. Doublet of Feld.

verb:vorliebnehmen.tx: From earlier vorlieb nehmen, from even earlier fürlieb nehmen, from a univerbation of für and lieb, literally "to take for dear". Compare lieber (“rather, preferably”).

verb:verdrücken.tx: From Middle High German verdrücken, verdrucken, from Old High German firdrukken. Equivalent to ver- + drücken.

noun:Vorwerk.tx: From Middle High German vorwërc (whence also Polish folwark). By surface analysis, vor + Werk. Compare Dutch voorwerk.

verb:vegetieren.tx: From Latin vegetāre, from vegetus, from vegēre, equivalent to Latin vegetus + -ieren.

verb:verschnüren.tx: From Middle High German versnüeren, from Old High German firsnuoren. Equivalent to ver- + schnüren.

verb:verramschen.tx: ver- + ramschen (“to buy for cheap”), probably by analogy to verbs like verkaufen, 19th century.

pt: to send, to ship, to dispatch
noun:Versender.tx: versenden (“to send, to ship, to dispatch”) + -er

verb:verzehnfachen.tx: zehnfach + ver- -en. See ver- -fachen for more.

verb:verhundertfachen.tx: hundertfach + ver- -en. See ver- -fachen for more.

verb:verenden.tx: From Middle High German verenden, from Old High German firentōn. Equivalent to ver- + enden.

verb:verbrühen.tx: From Middle High German verbrüejen, from Old High German firbruoen. Equivalent to ver- + brühen.

verb:verrücken.tx: From Middle High German verrücken, verrucken, virrucken, verrocken, ferrücken, ferrucken, from Old High German firrucken, firrukken, from Proto-West Germanic *frarukkijan, equivalent to ver- + rücken (“to move”). Cognate with Middle Low German vörrücken (> German Low German verrücken), Dutch verrukken, Saterland Frisian ferrukke, ferrukje.

verb:verheddern.tx: 18th century, borrowed from Low German verheddern, derived from Middle Low German hêde (“tow, hards”), from Proto-West Germanic *heʀdā. By surface analysis, ver- + Hede + -ern. The shortened vowel is due to the influence of -er- (as in Mutter and various other words).

noun:Vorbedacht.tx: Nominalization of the past participle of vorbedenken.

pt: fly on the top of a ship showing wind direction
verb:verklickern.tx: Verklicker (“fly on the top of a ship showing wind direction”) + -n, from Low German. A similar notion is found in zeigen / wissen woher der Wind weht.

phrase:vom Regen in die Taufe.tx: From vom Regen in die Traufe, either by corruption because Traufe is a rather rare word nowadays or deliberately in a humorous manner, especially when the non-idiomatic meaning resurfaces because the particular misfortune has to do with water.

noun:Vormundschaft.tx: From Middle High German vormuntschaft, from Old High German foramuntscaf.

adj:vorwitzig.tx: From Middle High German virwitzec, from Old High German firiwizzīg (“curious”). By surface analysis, Vorwitz + -ig.

verb:vorstrecken.tx: From vor- + strecken. Cognate with English forestretch.

noun:Vokabular.tx: 18th century, learned borrowing from Latin vocabularium. By surface analysis, Vokabel + -ar.

verb:verblühen.tx: From Middle High German verblüejen, from Old High German firbluoen. Equivalent to ver- + blühen. Cognate with Dutch verbloeien.

phrase:von der Bettkante stoßen.tx: Literally, “to push off the edge of the bed”

noun:Vorgesetzter.tx: Nominalisation of vorgesetzt, the perfect participle of vorsetzen.

noun:Vorfrühling.tx: From vor- + Frühling. Compare Polish przedwiośnie.

verb:verheilen.tx: From Middle High German verheilen, from Old High German firheilēn. Equivalent to ver- + heilen.

verb:verrinnen.tx: From Middle High German verrinnen, from Old High German firrinnan. Equivalent to ver- + rinnen.

verb:verfrachten.tx: ver- + frachten, since the 17th century. By surface analysis, be- + Fracht + -en.

verb:verlöschen.tx: From Middle High German verleschen. Equivalent to ver- + löschen.

noun:Vorschein.tx: 14th century, deverbal from vorscheinen (“to become visible”), now replaced with hervorscheinen. By surface analysis, vor (“before”) + Schein (“shine”). Compare Dutch tevoorschijn.

verb:verdreschen.tx: From Middle High German *verdreschen, from Old High German firdrescan, firdreskan. Equivalent to ver- + dreschen.

verb:verschwitzen.tx: Middle High German verswitzen, by surface analysis, ver- + schwitzen.

verb:vermiesen.tx: ver- (verb prefix indicating completion) + mies (“poor, inferior”) + -en (verb suffix)

verb:verblöden.tx: From Middle High German verbloeden (“to intimidate”). After blöd (“timid”) had changed its meaning to “stupid”, reinterpreted as ver- (prefix indicating completion) + blöd (“foolish, stupid”) + -en (verb suffix).

verb:verreiben.tx: From Middle High German verrīben. Equivalent to ver- + reiben.

noun:Vollblut.tx: Calque of English full-blood, voll + Blut.

verb:vorwarnen.tx: From Middle High German furwarnen. Equivalent to vor- + warnen.

noun:Verflossener.tx: Nominalisation of verflossen (“former”, literally “flowed away, melted away”).

noun:Veterinärmedizin.tx: A compound of veterinär (“veterinary”) + Medizin (“medicine”). Compare Swedish veterinärmedicin.

verb:vorhängen.tx: From Middle High German vorhāhen. Equivalent to vor- + hängen.

adj:verschämt.tx: From the past participle of Middle High German verschemen (“to become ashamed”).

verb:vertrösten.tx: From Middle High German vertrœsten, from Old High German firtrōsten. Equivalent to ver- + trösten.

verb:vermahlen.tx: From Middle High German *vermaln, from Old High German firmalan. Equivalent to ver- + mahlen.

verb:verwaschen.tx: From Middle High German verwaschen, from Old High German firwaskan. Equivalent to ver- + waschen.

adj:verwaschen.tx: From Middle High German verwaschen, from Old High German firwaskan. Equivalent to ver- + waschen.

verb:verräumen.tx: Formally from Middle High German verrūmen (“to leave, to flee”). Equivalent to ver- + räumen.

verb:versteuern.tx: From Middle High German verstiuren. Equivalent to ver- + steuern.

noun:Verhafteter.tx: From verhaftet (“arrested”) + -er; a substantivization of verhaftet, past participle of verhaften.

verb:verrohen.tx: From ver- + roh + -en. Compare Swedish förråa.

adj:verhuscht.tx: Past passive participle of verhuschen (“to vanish”).

noun:Vertrauter.tx: Substantivization of vertraut, past participle of vertrauen.

noun:Variabilität.tx: Borrowed from French variabilité. By surface analysis, variabel + -ität.

noun:Vollversammlung.tx: From voll (“full, filled; complete”) + Versammlung (“assembly, meeting”).

verb:verschreien.tx: From Middle High German verschrīen. Equivalent to ver- + schreien.

noun:Voreinstellung.tx: From voreinstellen + -ung, further from vor- + einstellen + -ung.

noun:Voland.tx: Inherited from Middle High German vālant, vōlant.

prep:vonseiten.tx: From von + Seite, attested since XVIII century

noun:Volley.tx: From volley, borrowed from English volley.
